title: Take Home Salary Calculator Australia: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, multiply your hourly rate by 38 then by 52 to get annual gross pay; the calculator also estimates tax, Medicare, and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $59,280 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the casual loading rate and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. If you are a casual employee, your base rate is the award or minimum rate, and the loading is added. Our calculator has a checkbox to add 25% casual loading – do not enter a rate that already includes loading.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated and is it included in my take-home pay?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings, currently at 12% of your gross pay (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830). It is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional contribution to your super fund. Our calculator shows the estimated super amount separately.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Use the Take Home Salary Calculator Australia

Welcome to the **take home salary calculator Australia** – your tool for turning an hourly rate or a salary offer into a clear annual picture. Whether you are negotiating a job, comparing offers, or planning your budget, this calculator helps you understand gross pay, tax, Medicare, and superannuation. All calculations are based on a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year, unless you adjust the hours.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

The foundation of any annual salary estimate is simple: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the Fair Work Ombudsman considers 38 hours per week as the standard. So if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay is:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

This formula assumes you work the same hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point. Our [the timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and see the annual figure instantly.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many industries have award rates that are higher. For example, the average full-time adult ordinary time earnings, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics (May 2026), are $2,083.70 per week – that is about $54.83 per hour for a 38-hour week. All employees (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. These are averages, not medians for a specific job. For job-specific pay, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. Our calculator includes a checkbox to add 25% casual loading. **Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the calculator add it for you. For the minimum wage, the casual rate is $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25).

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your salary; it is an additional contribution. Our calculator estimates the super amount separately. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Medicare

Your take-home pay depends on tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on the excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on the excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on the excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on the excess over $190,000

The Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Our calculator uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this tool’s update. The calculator does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a detailed breakdown, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page.

### Why a Fortnightly View Helps

Many Australians are paid fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by two. For example, if your weekly gross is $1,004.90 (minimum wage), your fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. The calculator shows both weekly and fortnightly figures to help you budget. You can also use our [pay guides](/blog) for award-specific information.

### Important Limitations

This calculator provides an estimate only. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For official rates, always check the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Taxation Office.

### Start Calculating Now

Ready to see your numbers? Visit [the timesheet](/) to enter your hourly rate and choose whether to add casual loading. Then use the annual, fortnightly, tax, and super results. The **take home salary calculator Australia** is designed for clarity – no guesswork, just your figures.

### Summary of Key Figures

- National Minimum Wage (1 July 2026): $26.44/hr, $1,004.90/week for 38 hours
- Casual rate: $33.05/hr (including 25% loading
- ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026): full-time adult ordinary time $2,083.70/week
- Super: 12% on top, up to $270,830
- Tax: 2026–27 resident scale

For more reference tables, see our [reference tables](/data) and [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage).

**Disclaimer:** This article uses the on-site reference figures as provided. They are not a job median. If the reference is an industry or state average, it is an average and not this job's median.
